2_RNG_generator_device_mismatch_fix.symptom: trainer.updater.load_state_dict() raised 'Expected a CPUGeneratorImplState of size 5056 but found the input RNG state size to be 16' when warm-starting a --device cpu run from the sealed B3-3 checkpoint (which was saved on --device cuda).
2_RNG_generator_device_mismatch_fix.root_cause: torch.Generator state format is device-family-specific and has NO defined cross-family conversion: a CPU generator's Mersenne-Twister state is always 5056 bytes; a CUDA generator's Philox seed+offset state is always 16 bytes. This is a deterministic property of the checkpoint's save-device vs. the load-device, not flakiness -- direct inspection confirmed the checkpoint's saved z_separation_generator tensor is exactly 16 bytes (torch.Size([16]), uint8).
2_RNG_generator_device_mismatch_fix.impact_scope: z_separation_generator only feeds SeparationObjective's subsampling (rl/custom_ppo/update/separation_objectives.py), which returns 'inactive' whenever z_idx is None -- i.e. whenever use_latent_strategy=False, as in every 4v4 specialist run including this one. Restoring or not restoring this generator's state has ZERO behavioural effect for this experiment; the crash was pure infrastructure breakage, not a correctness issue in the entity-repair architecture.
2_RNG_generator_device_mismatch_fix.fix: rl/custom_ppo/update/updater.py::PPOUpdater.load_state_dict -- compare state sizes explicitly; on a size mismatch, keep the freshly cfg.seed-derived generator and print a diagnostic instead of raising.
2_RNG_generator_device_mismatch_fix.tests_added: tests/test_ppo_updater_refactor_phase1.py::test_separation_generator_cross_device_family_mismatch_skips_restore (new) alongside the pre-existing same-device round-trip test (test_separation_generator_roundtrip), which still passes unchanged -- proving the fix is additive, not a behaviour change for the common case.

3_warm_start_is_initialization_not_resum.why_this_was_needed: 4V4_ENTITY_REPAIR_SPEC.json commits (held_fixed) to 'same training budget (steps) as the sealed B3-3 4v4 baseline'. The existing --load-path code path called trainer.load(path), which unconditionally restored global_step/updates_completed/return-norm stats/PPO-updater RNG state/comm+curriculum state FROM THE CHECKPOINT -- i.e. treated warm start as run CONTINUATION. Since B3-3's own global_step is 1,001,472, this meant either total_timesteps had to be set to 2,001,472 (a silent DOUBLE budget, discovered and flagged mid-session) or, if total_timesteps was left at a value appropriate for a from-scratch run, the trainer's own `while global_step < total_timesteps` loop was immediately false -- the exact silent no-op run this session's first launcher attempt actually produced (empty metrics.csv, no checkpoint delta, only pre-training manifest files).

fix.loader: rl/custom_ppo/checkpoints/loader.py::load_trainer_checkpoint gained reset_progress: bool = False. When True: global_step, updates_completed, return_norm/strategy_return_norm stats, last_stats, the PPO updater's full state_dict (z_separation_generator, exp2 teacher state), comm_runtime state, and v6i1 curriculum state are all left at the values CustomPPOTrainer.__init__ already gave this run, instead of being overwritten from the checkpoint. Model weights (and, separately, optimizer state via the pre-existing allow_active_actor_module_migration mechanism, now also forced when reset_progress=True) still load normally. rl/custom_ppo/trainer.py::load() and rl/training/initialization.py::maybe_load_checkpoint thread the flag through.
fix.CLI: experiments/train_specialist_scale.py sets cfg.warm_start_reset_progress = True in the --load-path branch (warm start from a DIFFERENT completed run) and leaves it False in the --resume branch (crash recovery of THIS run) -- exactly the distinction the docstring for --load-path already drew ('Distinct from --resume, which is for crash recovery of THIS run'), now enforced in the state that actually gets restored, not only in which checkpoint directory is accepted.

PI_decision_trail: First asked: how much ADDITIONAL budget on top of the carried-over global_step. PI chose +1,000,000 additional (i.e. total_timesteps=2,001,472).

On reading 4V4_ENTITY_REPAIR_SPEC.json's own frozen wording ('same training budget (steps) as the sealed B3-3 baseline'), flagged the conflict: +1,000,000 additional gives DOUBLE the baseline's budget, not the SAME budget the spec already committed to.
Re-asked with the conflict disclosed. PI chose to honor the frozen spec literally: reset global_step to 0 at warm start, 1,000,000 total (fresh) steps.

PI then independently confirmed and generalized this via a mid-turn message: '--load-path / --init-from' should reset global_step, optimizer state, scheduler state, rollout state, and training RNG/seeds, while '--resume' should preserve all of them -- weights are initialization, not continuation. The implementation above matches this generalization (optimizer state reset already existed via allow_active_actor_module_migration; rollout state -- _last_obs/_last_global_state/latent_state.current_z -- was ALREADY unconditionally reset on every load regardless of this flag; scheduler behaviour follows for free from global_step+total_timesteps both being fresh, since no separate persisted scheduler object exists in this codebase).
